_readme: Tunable parameters for דין דיוני question generation from real judgments.
Edit this file instead of the code, then re-run scripts/diuni/generate-diuni-set.mjs.
CLI flags (e.g. --effort=max, --count=3) override anything set here.
NOT tunable here, by design: the grounding rules. A question must be answerable
from the judgment it was built on, and every quote must appear in that judgment
verbatim. Those live in the generator because loosening them would silently
produce plausible questions with invented law instead of failing loudly.

authoring.register: SCOPE THIS TO THE FACT PATTERN ONLY. Write the scenario the way the Bar's own papers do — third person, plain procedural Hebrew, named parties (עו"ד לוי, משה, החברה), concrete steps in the order they happened. State what each side did and what the court decided, and stop. Do not name the doctrine, do not signpost which rule applies, do not hint at the answer: identifying the governing rule IS the question. Everything else — the stem, the analysis, the explanation, the distractor analysis — stays in precise legal Hebrew.
authoring.extra_instructions: The four options must be genuinely competitive: each wrong one should be the answer a candidate reaches by making ONE identifiable mistake — wrong forum, wrong stage of the proceeding, right rule applied to the wrong party, or a rule that exists but does not govern these facts. Never write a filler option that nobody would pick. WORDING: introduce every calendar date with בתאריך, never with ביום. Leave the fixed expression בו ביום alone.

_options.model.id: any current Claude model id; claude-opus-5 recommended for legal Hebrew
_options.model.max_tokens: hard ceiling on thinking + answer together. Raise if output truncates
_options.model.effort: low | medium | high | xhigh | max — controls depth and cost
_options.generation.prompt_cache: true caches the system+exemplars prefix; the 2nd question onward is much cheaper
_options.structure.answer_distribution.mode: rotate | none. rotate walks `sequence` so the correct answer lands on a different letter each question — left to itself the model favours one letter, and on a 40-question paper a candidate who always guesses it would score far above chance. The rotation continues across runs (it counts what is already in generated/), so a second batch does not restart at the first letter
_options.structure.answer_distribution.sequence: the cycle. ['א','ב','ג','ד'] spreads evenly; repeat a letter to weight it
_options.structure.variations_360: how many Q&A cards חשיבה 360° carries. The panel parses whatever it is given; 4 is the current product decision
_options.structure.fact_pattern_chars: guard rails, not targets — the generator rejects outside this range
_options.selection.order: balanced | random | newest | oldest. balanced spreads the batch across judgment_area_id and, weighted higher, the docket category — random over the whole table LOOKS spread and is not: it drew 7 of 11 judgments from תק (small claims), a category that is 22% of the pool, and every small-claims judgment ends with the same appeal-rights paragraph, which is what made 7 of 13 questions ask how to appeal. Counts are seeded from drafts already written so a second batch continues the spread
_options.grounding.mix: how a batch splits between the two kinds of source. The counts are worked out for the batch and then SHUFFLED, so the ratio is guaranteed while which question is which is not — pure per-question randomness would let a run of ten come out all one kind. Set { verdict: 1, law: 0 } for verdicts only
_options.grounding.law.min_section_chars: skip statutory sections too short to build a question from. A one-line definition has nothing to test
_options.grounding.law.max_section_chars: skip sections so long they are really a chapter; the model would pick its own topic out of them and the question stops being about a rule
_options.grounding.law.only_law_ids / exclude_law: Knesset law ids (mahoti_laws.law_id), e.g. [2000798] for חוק לשכת עורכי הדין. Empty = no filter
_options.selection.min_text_chars: skip judgments too short to build a question from
_options.selection.only_areas / exclude_areas: judgment_area_id slugs, e.g. ['banking_law']. Empty = no filter
_options.selection.min_confidence: null | low | medium | high — the classifier's own confidence in the area label
_options.exemplars.count: how many real Bar questions are shown as style anchors. Cached, so each one costs ~0.006c per question to re-read — 10 is ~15c per 40-question run. Few-shot returns flatten past ~15
_options.exemplars.pick: balanced | form | spread | first | random. balanced spreads on TWO axes — stem form and the statute the answer key cites — because diversifying phrasing alone concentrated the subject: 10 form-diverse anchors produced a batch where 8 of 13 questions asked how to appeal a judgment. form is that earlier strategy, kept so the comparison can be re-run. spread is the original positional sample
_options.authoring.register: free text — the voice of the fact pattern
_options.authoring.extra_instructions: free text appended to the prompt — the main tuning knob
_options.validation.require_verbatim_quote: every cited passage must appear in the judgment character for character (after whitespace normalisation). Turning this off removes the only mechanical check that the question is grounded in real law
_options.validation.forbid_verdict_identifiers: reject a question whose fact pattern leaks the case number or party names — a candidate who can search the judgment is not answering the question
